verses.text: “At that time,” says Yahweh, “they shall bring out the bones of the kings of Judah, and the bones of his princes, and the bones of the priests, and the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, out of their graves;

and they shall spread them before the sun, and the moon, and all the army of the sky, which they have loved, and which they have served, and after which they have walked, and which they have sought, and which they have worshiped: they shall not be gathered, nor be buried, they shall be for dung on the surface of the earth.
Death shall be chosen rather than life by all the residue that remain of this evil family, that remain in all the places where I have driven them,” says Yahweh of Armies.
“Moreover you shall tell them, ‘Yahweh says: “‘Shall men fall, and not rise up again? Shall one turn away, and not return?
Why then have the people of Jerusalem fallen back by a perpetual backsliding? They cling to deceit, they refuse to return.
I listened and heard, but they didn’t say what is right. No one repents of his wickedness, saying, “What have I done?” Everyone turns to his course, as a horse that rushes headlong in the battle.
Yes, the stork in the sky knows her appointed times; and the turtledove, the swallow, and the crane observe the time of their coming; but my people don’t know Yahweh’s law.
“‘How do you say, “We are wise, and Yahweh’s law is with us?” But, behold, the false pen of the scribes has worked falsely.
The wise men are disappointed. They are dismayed and trapped. Behold, they have rejected Yahweh’s word. What kind of wisdom is in them?

Therefore will I give their wives to others, and their fields to those who shall possess them. For everyone from the least even to the greatest is given to covetousness; from the prophet even to the priest everyone deals falsely.
They have healed the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, “Peace, peace,” when there is no peace.

Were they ashamed when they had committed abomination? No, they were not at all ashamed, neither could they blush: therefore they shall fall among those who fall; in the time of their visitation they shall be cast down, says Yahweh.
“‘I will utterly consume them, says Yahweh: no grapes shall be on the vine, nor figs on the fig tree, and the leaf shall fade; and the things that I have given them shall pass away from them.’”

“Why do we sit still? Assemble yourselves, and let us enter into the fortified cities, and let us be silent there; for Yahweh our God has put us to silence, and given us water of gall to drink, because we have sinned against Yahweh.
We looked for peace, but no good came; and for a time of healing, and behold, dismay!

The snorting of his horses is heard from Dan: at the sound of the neighing of his strong ones the whole land trembles; for they have come, and have devoured the land and all that is in it; the city and those who dwell therein.”
“For, behold, I will send serpents, adders among you, which will not be charmed; and they shall bite you,” says Yahweh.
Oh that I could comfort myself against sorrow! My heart is faint within me.

Behold, the voice of the cry of the daughter of my people from a land that is very far off: “Isn’t Yahweh in Zion? Isn’t her King in her?” “Why have they provoked me to anger with their engraved images, and with foreign vanities?”
“The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved.”
For the hurt of the daughter of my people am I hurt: I mourn; dismay has taken hold on me.
Is there no balm in Gilead? is there no physician there? Why then isn’t the health of the daughter of my people recovered?

footnotes.content: What a terrible picture—bones dragged into the sun, stripped of the honor of burial. Yet I'm struck that even Judah's unfaithfulness cannot change God's long reach. He sees everything, forgets nothing, and even in judgment speaks plain truth. There's a tenderness in that clarity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bones scattered like refuse—a sign that what we love and chase instead of the Lord ends in shame. The sky and sun and moon couldn't save those who served them. Only He who made the heavens holds anything together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even the remnant chooses death over return. That breaks my heart—not because God fails them, but because they choose exile from Him. I've learned that sometimes people would rather suffer anywhere than turn around. Yet He leaves the door open still.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God's question cuts through the fog: don't men naturally rise after a fall? Don't they turn back to the path they lost? It's true. We're made for return. Yet Jerusalem has done neither. I hear sorrow in the Lord's voice here—grief over a people who've stopped reaching.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Perpetual backsliding—that phrase haunts me. Not one stumble, but a stubborn walking away, choosing deceit over truth. When I've done the same, I've learned it takes more strength to keep running from God than to stop and confess. Pride always makes us lie.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I hear the Lord's heartbreak—He listened for the words that never came. Not 'forgive us' but silence and rush headlong into sin like a war-horse with no rider. There's a name for that posture: it's what we choose when we won't let Him lead.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The stork and the crane know their seasons—they hear the call in their blood and obey. But Israel doesn't know God's law, though it's written on their hearts. Animals honor their nature; we honor ours only when we remember we belong to the One who made us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They say 'We are wise, and God's law is with us'—yet the scribes' pen has twisted it. How easy to wrap our own desires in Scripture's name and call it wisdom. I've seen that poison in my own day. The only guard against it is to let the Word read us, not the other way around.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The wise are trapped by their own wisdom—they've rejected the Lord's word and now sit dismayed, their cleverness useless. I've watched smart people outsmart themselves into a corner. True wisdom begins when we stop defending ourselves and start listening.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wives and fields to others—loss from the least to the greatest. And why? Because everyone, from prophet to priest, deals falsely. When we trade integrity for gain, we lose the one thing that holds a house together: trust. God doesn't leave you broke—you leave yourself there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Peace, peace, when there is no peace—false healers speaking comfort over a wound still bleeding. I've heard it said, and said it myself: easier to numb than to feel the truth that might set us free. Real healing starts with admitting the hurt.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They're not ashamed—not even a blush. When shame dies, so does the way back. I've seen that hardness in people, and it breaks my heart. Yet the Lord keeps calling anyway, keeps warning, because even at the edge of judgment there's still time for one more turn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No grapes on the vine, no figs on the tree—the orchard that once bore fruit now stands bare. It's what happens when we pull ourselves away from the Root. The Lord doesn't take our gifts; we let them slip through our fingers when we stop belonging to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Why sit still? The people run to their walls, their strongholds—hoping walls will save them now that they've silenced the Lord within. I know that panic. We reach for safety everywhere but where it lives: in the arms of the One we've tried to escape.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They looked for peace but found dismay—the gap between what we hope for and what we get when we've lost the only Peace-giver. No balm, no physician, just the empty ache. I've tasted that myself, in seasons when I turned away.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sound of horses from Dan—the north—an ancient terror route. Everything trembles when the invader comes. But I wonder: did they tremble when the Lord called them? Did the thunder of His word move them the way war-horses' hooves finally do?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Serpents and adders—creatures that won't be charmed by our words or rituals. Sometimes judgment comes not as loud thunder but as quiet slithering, things we can't control or smooth-talk away. It's a hard mercy: the world won't bend to our will.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah's heart is faint—he has carried the Lord's word for so long while his people don't listen. Readers today hear an echo in those who preach repentance and see only hardened faces. Yet they keep speaking anyway, because the Lord's work isn't measured by who hears.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The daughter of Zion cries out from far away: 'Isn't the King here? Isn't Yahweh in Zion?' Yet they've chased carved images instead. A people can feel abandoned by their God only when they've abandoned Him first. The King is always here—we're the ones who leave.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The harvest is past, summer is ended, and they are not saved. There's a tender urgency in those words—the seasons came and went, but they didn't turn in time. I think of how many harvests of mercy God sends, how long He waits for us to notice He's still reaching.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I am hurt for the hurt of my people—those are the Lord's words, but they could be Jeremiah's too. The prophet grieves with God over the wound his people have chosen. That's intercession: feeling the ache of those who won't turn, because you see what they could be.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Is there no balm in Gilead? Gilead—a real place, famous for its healing oils and physicians. Yet the only cure they need is the one they refuse: to turn back and be healed by the Physician who is always waiting. The remedy is as close as confession.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
